title: Manual-review moderation observability playbook
body:
Purpose
This playbook defines the observability surface for flows that involve automated moderation + optional human review. Focus is on three outcomes: (1) detecting model-caused escalations to human queues, (2) ensuring reviewer throughput and SLA for label delivery, and (3) attributing cost & quality impact to routing/threshold changes.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to hosted and dedicated deployments but contains privacy notes for Private/VPC installs.
- Human-review path is an async queue (job service) with fairness/priority tiers.
- We assume existing request tracing from API gateway through router to model runtime; this doc extends span semantics for the reviewer subsystem.

High-level signal categories (why we need them)
- Model->Escalation signals: frequency and false positive/negative trends that drive human load.
- Reviewer operational signals: queue depth, assignment latency, median/95th label latency, and abandonment rate.
- Quality signals: reviewer agreement rate vs model label, regression in reviewer sentiment, rework loops (reassigned items).
- Cost signals: tokens consumed for moderation, human-minute cost per event, model fallback rate and downstream inference re-runs.

Metric definitions (canonical names + intent)
- moderation.model.escalation_rate (ratio): number of requests routed to human review / total moderation requests. Window: 1m, 1h, 24h.
- moderation.model.false_escalation_rate (ratio): escalations where human verdict = allow. Window: rolling 7d.
- moderation.model.missed_escalation_rate (ratio): cases where model allowed but later flagged by reviewer or user report. Window: rolling 7d.
- moderation.queue.depth (gauge): number of items pending review by priority tier. Tags: priority, region, tenant_id.
- moderation.queue.time_to_assign_pct50/90/99 (histogram/quantiles): time from enqueue -> assignment.
- moderation.review.latency_pct50/90/99 (histogram): time from assignment -> completed label.
- moderation.review.abandonment_rate (ratio): assigned but not completed within TTL / assigned.
- moderation.review.reassign_rate (ratio): items re-assigned at least once / completed.
- moderation.quality.inter_annotator_agreement (ratio): fraction of double-reviewed items where labels match.
- moderation.cost.token_per_event (counter): tokens consumed per moderation request (model_op token count).
- moderation.cost.human_min_per_event (histogram): human-minutes spent per reviewed item.
- moderation.routing.fallback_rate (ratio): percent of requests routed away from primary model to fallback variants.
- moderation.privacy.redaction_rate (ratio): fraction of traces with PII redaction flagged.

Tagging conventions and cardinality control
- Required tags: tenant_id (if applicable), region, priority (low|normal|high), model_variant, route_policy.
- Avoid high-cardinality user_id and freeform text in metrics. Use sample-based traces for per-user debug.
- For coarser dashboards, use tenant cohorts (enterprise|midmarket|plg) instead of raw tenant ids.

Tracing span model (span names + key attributes)
- span: api.request - attrs: request_id, tenant_id, user_agent, client_route
- span: moderation.router - attrs: decision, threshold_used, model_variant, fallback_candidate
- span: model.infer - attrs: model_name, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, quantization_profile
- span: moderation.queue.enqueue - attrs: queue_id, priority, enqueue_ts
- span: reviewer.assignment - attrs: reviewer_id (pseudonymized), assignment_ts, batch_id
- span: reviewer.action - attrs: action (allow|block|escalate), action_ts, review_latency_ms
- span: review.audit.persist - attrs: audit_id, storage_tier
- Correlate sampler: set trace.sample_rate dynamically for items with escalations, high-cost token usage, or flagged PII.

Sampling strategy
- Base traces: 0.5% global to control ingest cost.
- Exceptional traces: 100% sampling for any request that: routes to human review, uses > 2x median tokens, triggers fallback, or is part of a canary experiment.
- Privacy-sensitive traces: redact PII at collection time, store only metadata and sanitized text. Use policy tag moderation.privacy.redaction_rate to track effectiveness.

Dashboards (layout + suggested panels)
- Summary row (top): overall escalations/hr, queue depth (total), median review latency, tokens/hr, human-minutes/hr.
- Escalation trends: time-series for escalation_rate and false_escalation_rate (configurable smoothing), overlay major routing changes.
- Queue health: stacked area by priority for queue.depth, heatmap of assign latency by hour of day, histogram of review.latency.
- Cost & throughput: tokens_per_event median/90, tokens/hr, human_min_per_event trend, cost_estimate panel (token_cost * tokens/hr + human_rate * human_minutes/hr). Include currency toggle.
- Quality dashboard: inter_annotator_agreement, reassign_rate, missed_escalation_rate, per-model_variant confusion matrix snapshot (periodic sample).
- Investigation panel: breadcrumbs linking trace ids for recent escalations, sample payload (sanitized), last reviewer comment.
- Alerting/Oncall row: queue.depth>threshold by priority, review.latency_pct90>SLO, false_escalation_rate spike > baseline*3.

SLO proposals (initial targets)
- reviewer.label_latency: 90th percentile <= 300s for priority=high, <= 900s for normal.
- escalation_false_rate: <= 10% monthly for consumer tenants; <= 5% for enterprise tier.
- queue.abandonment_rate: < 1% weekly.
- sample coverage SLO: Exceptional traces captured for 99% of escalations.

Alerting guidance and runbook snippets
- Alert: queue.depth.high - trigger when depth_high_priority > 50 for 5m. Pager to ops owner and cs-coverage.
- Alert: review.latency.p95 - trigger when p95 > SLO for 10m and sustained trend for 30m. Triage: check reviewer availability, reassign spikes, broker errors.
- Alert: false_escalation.spike - trigger on 3x baseline in 1h. Triage: check recent model rollout, threshold flips, dataset drift.

Privacy & retention notes
- Traces containing PII must be redacted at collector. Use deterministic hashing for reviewer_id and tenant_id where needed.
- Retention: full traces for escalations kept 90d; sanitized traces for sampled events kept 365d for model quality analysis.
- For Private deployments, recommend local-only trace storage + aggregated metrics export to Redwood control plane under customer's opt-in.

Dashboards ownership & lifecycle
- Owners: obs-moderation (primary), obs-infra (support). Tag dashboards with owner and review cadence (weekly for queue, monthly for quality).
- Deprecation: if an upstream routing change removes a metric, owners must mark dashboards deprecated and provide migration notes in Confluence.

Operational play examples
- Rapid false-positive regression: throttle new routing, rollback to previous model_variant, increase sampling of escalations, run batch audit of last 1k escalations for root cause.
- Sustained queue growth: temporarily raise routing threshold, enable overflow reviewers (SLA-based), create surge alert, and start cost-impact analysis.

Open decisions / questions (for next review)
- Should we store reviewer notes text in metric stores or only in audit blob? (privacy vs. searchability).
- Cohort-based SLOs: how many tenants need bespoke targets?
- Cost attribution granularity: per-tenant real-time vs nightly batch?

Appendix: quick queries (pseudocode)
- Escalation rate by model: SELECT sum(escalated)/count(*) FROM moderation WHERE time_bucket = '1h' GROUP BY model_variant
- P95 review latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(moderation_review_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))

Notes and acknowledgements
- Drafted by: Sophia Li (obs), reviewed by Raj Patel (moderation), Marta Gomez (privacy), Liam O'Connor (sre).
- Follow-up: align tags with global metric registry (obs-metric-standards), schedule walkthrough with CS and product next sprint.

End of document
